name: J. Ignacio Mestre
bio: I'm a postdoctoral researcher at Universitat Politècnica de València, where I work on making AI systems efficient and sustainable to deploy. I like research that ships: when an idea works, I turn it into a library other people can install and use.

I received my Ph.D. in Computer Science from Universitat Jaume I in 2026 (cum laude, International Doctorate mention) with the thesis “Advances in Training and Inference Optimizations for Efficient Deep Neural Networks”, advised by Manuel F. Dolz and José Duato. During my Ph.D. I was part of the HPC&A group at UJI and a visiting researcher at the University of Glasgow.

software.name: AnyInit
software.description: Initialize any deep neural network correctly with one call. AnyInit traces the model, detects the activation that follows each layer, and scales every weight so the signal neither vanishes nor explodes. Works with PyTorch, Keras 3 and Flax, and supports custom activations and arbitrary architectures.

software.name: Sinusoidal Initialization
software.description: Official PyTorch implementation of our NeurIPS 2025 paper. A deterministic initialization that builds structured weight matrices from sinusoids, improving convergence speed and final accuracy across CNNs, vision transformers and LLMs.

research.title: Compressing and accelerating neural networks
research.description: Pruning, quantization, layer fusion and accuracy recovery to run deep models fast on GPUs, ARM/RISC-V CPUs and IoT devices.

research.title: Training dynamics
research.description: Weight initialization, regularization and overfitting detection, and what structural and quantitative knowledge ReLU networks actually learn.

research.title: Distributed & federated learning
research.description: Distributed training on GPU clusters and robust model aggregation in federated learning.

news.text: Two papers on federated learning accepted at FLICS 2026.
Defended my Ph.D. at Universitat Jaume I: cum laude, with International Doctorate mention.
Joined Universitat Politècnica de València as a postdoctoral researcher.
Presented “Sinusoidal Initialization, Time for a New Start” at NeurIPS 2025 in San Diego.
